q01:
Overall we are ahead of pace to date, but if nothing changes the program lands at 57329 doors on Election Day, 3303 short of the 60632 goal.
- Program: 33503 doors to date vs a goal to date of 32431, 103.3% of pace; projected 57329, which is 94.6% of goal, a shortfall of 3303 doors (projected_vs_goal -3303) [table:v_office_pace]
- Northside: 112.5% of pace; projected 23583 vs a goal of 22675, 908 over goal (104%) [table:v_office_pace]
- Harbor: 105.3% of pace; projected 19150 vs a goal of 20157, 1007 short (95%) [table:v_office_pace]
- Eastgate: 89.3% of pace, the only office behind; projected 14596 vs a goal of 17800, 3204 short (82%) [table:v_office_pace]
- How it's worked out: pace is doors to date vs goal to date; the projection is doors to date plus the last 7 days' average daily doors (1489.1 program-wide) times the 16 knocking days left [doc:program-plan#pace-and-projection]
q03:
Eastgate needs 4.4 more shifts a day, Harbor 1.3 and Northside none, or 4.1 more a day program-wide.
- Eastgate: 12.6 shifts a day needed vs 8.3 a day over the last 7 days, 4.4 extra [table:v_office_pace]
- Harbor: 11.1 needed vs 9.9 now, 1.3 extra [table:v_office_pace]
- Northside: 10.1 needed vs 11.1 now, 0 extra [table:v_office_pace]
- All offices: 33.3 needed vs 29.3 now, 4.1 extra [table:v_office_pace]
- How it's worked out: doors still needed divided by knocking days left, divided by the last 7 days' doors per shift; extra shifts is that minus the last 7 days' average shifts per day [doc:program-plan#shifts-needed]
q05:
Ask the client for more doors: our capacity for the rest of the program is larger than the untouched turf we have left, and a second pass should be the fallback.
- Capacity for the rest of the program: 23826 doors (1489.1 average daily doors over the last 7 days x 16 knocking days left) [table:v_office_pace]
- Untouched doors left in our turf: 10393 [table:v_turf_summary]
- Not-home doors available for a second pass: 18555 [table:v_turf_summary]
- Program projection is 57329 vs a 60632 goal, a 3303-door shortfall [table:v_office_pace]
- Rule: when capacity exceeds untouched doors, ask for more doors first, since new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate; second passes contact voters at roughly half that rate [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]
q07:
The client's report counts attempts before QC rollbacks, while our dashboard counts doors once per day with rollbacks removed; on Oct 12 the big gap is Eastgate, where 142 attempts were rolled back.
- Eastgate: client report 498 vs our 342 doors; 498 attempts, of which 142 were rolled back [table:client_daily_report] [table:v_daily_doors]
- Harbor: client report 428 vs our 406 doors; 428 attempts, 0 rolled back, so the gap is repeat attempts [table:client_daily_report] [table:v_daily_doors]
- Northside: client report 558 vs our 533 doors; 558 attempts, 0 rolled back [table:client_daily_report] [table:v_daily_doors]
- All offices: 1484 attempts vs 1281 doors, with 142 rolled-back attempts [table:v_daily_doors]
- How it's worked out: the gap on any day is repeat attempts at the same door plus attempts later rolled back; a normal day shows a few percent from repeats, and a larger gap almost always means a rollback [doc:counting-doors#why-the-client-s-numbers-differ-from-ours]
- The client's daily report is pulled at the end of each day as submitted, before any QC rollback, and we don't edit a daily report after it is sent [doc:client-reporting#daily-report]

x04:
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock, flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart.
- Threshold: 10 or more consecutive knocks, each under 30 seconds apart [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back, so those knocks no longer count as doors or contacts; a whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Rollbacks happen after the day's client report is pulled, so they never change a report already sent [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
- Every open flag needs a conversation with the field lead before the next shift; two or more flash knocking or householding flags in a week for one canvasser go to the field director [doc:qc-rules#what-happens-after-a-flag]
